materials/bronze: "does not spark when struck, so it suits work near flammable gases": non-sparking hand gear is usually specified in aluminium bronze or beryllium copper; true of copper alloys generally, but not a standard selling point of every tin bronze
"resists seawater, so it is used for ship propellers": large propellers are mostly nickel-aluminium bronze; the traditional 'manganese bronze' is metallurgically a brass
materials/cement: "is ground into a powder finer than most flour": typical cement particles are about 10-15 micrometres, wheat flour mostly larger; true as a general comparison, not for every flour grade
materials/marble: "can be slightly translucent where it is cut thin": true of fine white marbles; coarse or dark marbles are not noticeably translucent
